LESSON: CONSERVING ANIMAL FEED: HAY (BALED HAY MAKING, STANDING FORAGE, STACKING).

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: AGRICULTURE FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.1: Conserving Animal Feed: Hay (Baled hay making, standing forage, stacking).
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Conserving Animal Feed: Hay (Baled hay making, standing forage, stacking)., part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 AGRICULTURE FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How can hay conservation contribute to coping with drought? 2. Why do households conserve forage?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Conserving Animal Feed: Hay (Baled hay making, standing forage, stacking). together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and problem solving: The learner develops evaluation and decision-making skills as they analyse the drought

problem and apply the most applicable solution in the local context.

• Communication and collaboration: The learner develops signing and teamwork skills as they discuss ways of coping with drought

in the context of rearing animals.

Values:
• Unity: as the learner respects other’s opinion during group discussion and class presentations on how households can adopt

conservation of forage in coping with drought.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
• Disaster risk reduction: The learner analyses drought-related challenges in animal production and adopts coping mechanisms.

Links to other Learning Areas:
• Learners relate conservation of hay to concepts of mitigating effects of climate change learnt in Social Studies.

Suggested Learning Resources

• Digital devices.

• Sign language dictionary.

• Baled Hay.

• Stacked forage.
